rationale: Attempt-01 improved simulated latency from 316.97us to 232.89us using block_M=64, block_N=128, block_K=32, stage=2, threads=256, swizzle=8, confirming stage>=2 pipelining helped. Attempt-02 failed with a schema/model ValueError before evaluation; this revision restores a fully valid schema and keeps the confirmed-good structural region. Retaining block_M {32,64,128}, block_N {64,128,256}, block_K expanded to {32,64,128} to keep testing the block_K=128 hypothesis from attempt-01 that did not get exercised. Stages {1,2,3,4} retained so HiGHS can trade depth vs footprint under the 32KB cap (stage>=3 with block_K>=64 and block_M+block_N large will be footprint-limited). Threads still {128,256}; 64 remains excluded pending evidence that warp layout is underutilized. Swizzle expanded to the full {0,4,8,16,32,64}: attempt-01's swizzle=8 selection coincided with the gain, but reuse is an analytic hypothesis, so larger panels must be tested to see whether locality gains materialize or whether panels exceeding cache reduce benefit. Weights: traffic=1, pipeline=1, launches lowered to 0.5 (2048^3 already saturates the machine at modest tiles), footprint raised to 1.5 because baseline sat at the 32KB cap and deeper pipelines with wider block_K will hit the limit. Validation scope: Metal numerical checks execute exact source/TIR; CUDA binaries are not run; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements, and the proxy cost is a dimensionless ranking only. Next hypothesis: swizzle panels >8 and/or block_K=128 with stage 3-4 may further reduce simulated latency if locality and K-pipelining outweigh footprint; if larger swizzle values tie or underperform, revert to narrower panels and spend domain width on block_M/block_N/threads. No claim of global optimality is made.
